title: Great Buddha Statue - The Icon of Peace and Enlightenment
content:
Great Buddha Statue

The Great Buddha Statue in Bodh Gaya, Bihar, is one of the tallest and most magnificent statues of Lord Buddha in India. Standing at an impressive 25 meters (82 feet), it represents Buddha in a calm meditation posture, symbolizing peace, serenity, and enlightenment. It is a major attraction for pilgrims and travelers visiting Bodh Gaya.

History and Significance

The Great Buddha Statue was consecrated in 1989 by the 14th Dalai Lama. Built with the joint effort of Indian and Japanese artisans, the statue took over seven years to complete. It represents the spiritual connection between India and Japan and stands as a global symbol of Buddhism’s message of compassion and wisdom.

Design and Architecture

Made of sandstone and red granite, the statue shows Lord Buddha seated in a meditative posture (Dhyana Mudra) on a giant lotus. Surrounding the main figure are ten smaller statues of Buddha’s disciples, enhancing its divine beauty. The area around the statue is beautifully landscaped, creating a peaceful environment for reflection and meditation.

Best Time to Visit

The best time to visit the Great Buddha Statue is from October to March, when the weather is pleasant and ideal for sightseeing and photography.

Entry Fee and Timings

Entry Fee: Free for all visitors

Visiting Hours: 7:00 AM - 5:30 PM

How to Reach

  • By Air: Nearest airport - Gaya International Airport (12 km)
  • By Train: Nearest station - Gaya Junction (16 km)
  • By Road: Well connected by buses and taxis from Patna, Rajgir, and Nalanda.

Tips for Visitors

  • Visit early morning or late afternoon for peaceful vibes.
  • Don’t forget to take off your shoes before entering the main area.
  • Photography is allowed, but respect the sanctity of the place.
  • Spend a few minutes meditating for a calm experience.
